summaryDeep:
This person can make communication feel more complicated than either of you intends.

A casual comment picks up a tone you never meant. A simple question lands like criticism. You send a text that feels completely normal when you write it, only to discover it was received very differently on the other side. Before long, the conversation has drifted away from the original issue. Now you are trying to untangle what was said, how it was heard, and why the same misunderstanding seems to keep showing up between you.

This is the contact of crossed wires. Not because nobody cares. The problem is translation. Tone, timing, wording, assumptions. The small things that seem too minor to matter until they keep happening.

When this works, it asks both people to become more intentional with language. You cannot rely on assumptions or expect your words to carry the meaning you intended on their own. The invitation is to slow down and stay curious about the gap between your intention and their experience. Over time, you learn that good communication is not just about expressing yourself clearly. It is also about making sure the message lands.

The challenge is that repeated misunderstandings can slowly put both people on guard. Over time, you stop entering conversations with curiosity and start entering them with expectation. A normal question can sound like doubt. A pause can feel like judgment. A simple clarification can land as rejection. Before long, the conversation is carrying the weight of every previous misunderstanding before it has even had a chance to unfold.

This is where the real work begins. When communication breaks down, the temptation is to turn one difficult moment into a larger conclusion about the relationship. Resist that impulse. Slow the conversation down. Get curious before you get certain. Ask what they meant. Share what you heard. Check the story you are telling against what is actually happening. The goal is not perfect communication. The goal is to keep returning to clarity instead of punishing each other for the places where the message got distorted.
